{{short description|Danish mathematician}}

{{Use list-defined references|date=October 2020}}
'''Eva Bjørn Vedel Jensen''' (born 14 June 1951) is a Danish mathematician and statistician known for her work in [[spatial statistics]], [[stereology]], [[stochastic geometry]], and [[medical imaging]].{{r|stif}} She is a professor emeritus in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at [[Aarhus University]].{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
After earning a master's degree at [[Aarhus University]] in 1976,{{r|stif}} she became a faculty member at the university in 1979. She completed a doctorate at Aarhus in 1987,{{r|stif|cv}} and became full professor there in 2003.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Vedel Jensen has been an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] since 1992,{{r|cv|isi}} and is also a member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]].{{r|stif|kdvs}}

She won the Villum Kann Rasmussen Annual Award for Technical and Scientific Research of the [[Villum Foundation]] in 2009. She was named a knight of the [[Order of the Dannebrog]] in 2010.{{r|stif|prizes}} The [[University of Bern]] gave her an honorary doctorate in 2013.{{r|prizes|unibe}}

==Selected publications==
Vedel Jensen is the author of books including:
*''Local Stereology'' (World Scientific, 1998){{r|ls}}
*''Stereology for Statisticians'' (with [[Adrian Baddeley]], Chapman & Hall/CRC, 2005){{r|s4s}}

She has also written several highly cited papers with [[Hans Jørgen G. Gundersen]] including:
